title: kv-pressure-driven-partial-compact-and-spill-smoothing
author: Anika Sharma
description: Motivation: Under high write-heavy inference workloads the KV cache shows repeated small spill events and high fragmentation which increases device-to-host paging and amplifies downstream latency spikes. This PR introduces a two-part mitigation: a pressure-driven partial compaction pass that opportunistically coalesces adjacent freelist segments without doing full in-place compaction, and a spill-smoothing controller that rate-limits spillback by applying a moving-average based backpressure signal to the request scheduler. Design summary: 1) Partial compactor: a lightweight, incremental compaction routine that runs per-tenant when fragmentation_ratio > configurable_threshold. It scans small contiguous free ranges (configurable max_range_bytes) and merges them into larger slabs by doing local pointer adjustments and an optional small memcpy for adjacent live slots. The pass is bounded by budget (time_slices_per_epoch, bytes_moved_per_epoch) to keep p99 latency impact minimal. 2) Pressure-driven reservation: when device resident memory pressure exceeds a high watermark the allocator reserves a small eviction buffer per-tenant to avoid thrashing; the buffer size is adaptive (feedback loop tied to recent spill bytes and request QPS). 3) Spill-smoothing controller: computes an exponential moving average of spill_rate and uses a PID-inspired dampener to produce a spill_budget token rate consumed by the scheduler. When budget is exhausted the scheduler shifts requests to non-blocking paths or short-circuits to a lower-capacity model variant. 4) Telemetry and knobs: added kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.partial_compact_runs, kv.cache.spill_budget_ratio, and a feature flag kv.partial_compact.enabled. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind runtime flag, staged rollout to internal canaries (10% traffic) for 48h, followed by 50% then full. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4621) - [x] unit tests for compactor/allocator - [x] integration test with simulated fragmentation - [x] canary run and perf observations - [x] CI green and load-tested on perf-lab Results: On perf-lab synthetic mixed read/write workload (80% read, 20% write) with heavy hotspotting, spill frequency reduced by ~34% and host paging bytes decreased by ~1.6x. End-to-end p99 generation latency improved ~12% under 95th percentile memory pressure scenarios. Caveats: partial compaction moves small amounts of memory and does not replace a full defragmentation for extreme fragmentation cases; the spill-smoothing tradeoff may route some requests to lower-quality variants under sustained pressure. References: Linear ENG-4621 (partial compactor), ENG-4702 (spill smoothing), linked incident SUP-3121 for root cause analysis.

review_comments: Liam: Overall looks solid, a couple of questions on safety of pointer adjustments in the compactor when GC-like concurrent readers may be scanning. Can we document invariants and add an assert in debug builds?
Author (Anika): Added a defensive epoch check and an assert in debug builds; compactor now acquires a per-segment lightweight pin to prevent races (see partial_compactor.rs).
Mei: How does the spill budget interact with tenant burst policies? Could it starve short-lived spikes?
Author (Anika): Budget window reduced to 250ms for burst tolerance and we added a burst token reserve tied to tenant SLA. Measured no starvation in canary. See reservation_controller.rs comments.
Rafael: CI flakes in linux-integration on the first run (timing issue). Rerun fixed it; consider increasing test timeout for the fragmentation harness.
Author (Anika): Increased harness timeout and added a retry hook; CI stable on rerun.

performance_summary: Synthetic perf-lab (mixed workload, hotspotting): spill events reduced by 34%
Host paging bytes decreased by 1.6x during peak
End-to-end p99 generation latency improved by 12% under high memory pressure
CPU cost increase: +2% median (compaction work amortized), GPU unaffected
release_notes: Introduced a bounded partial compactor and spill-smoothing controller to reduce KV cache spill frequency and lower host paging under pressure. Config knobs: kv.partial_compact.enabled, kv.partial_compact.max_range_bytes, kv.spill_smoothing.window_ms. Default is disabled for older clusters; enabled in new deployments.
notes_for_operators: To enable on a cluster: set kv.partial_compact.enabled=true in runtime config and monitor kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio and kv.cache.spill_budget_ratio.
If you observe increased CPU without spill reduction, reduce kv.partial_compact.time_slices_per_epoch or increase max_range_bytes.
Fallback: feature can be toggled off without restarting serving processes; graceful drain of compactor state occurs within configured epoch windows.
